label: alg:per-isotope-binding
title: Per-isotope binding $B(K) = m_e \cdot \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda \Delta_\lambda$
html:
Algorithm (Per-isotope binding energy — experimental q-difference generating-function model; the \Delta_\lambda magnitude is open). Evaluate the binding energy B_n \propto w_n for multi-body nuclear clusters via the universal CKRecursion depth-2 discrete generating function, seeded by the topological traces of the strong mediator knots.

Input

  • Topological trace constants: r_{\mathrm{gluonic}} = 3 and r_{\mathrm{residual}} = 2.5.
  • The universal bar-even structural prior a_0 = 1/2.
  • SU(4)/S_3 isospin representation anomaly shifts (e.g., +1.4947 m_e).

Output

  • Predicted binding energy B_n in MeV.

Algorithm

1. Compute the exact residual trace r_{res} evaluated at the substrate root q_0 (yields ~2.596).
2. Seed the depth-2 CKRecursion engine: w_{n+1} = 0.5 * w_n + r_{res} * w_{n-1}.
3. The engine natively generates the multi-body binding hierarchy (w_2 = 4.35, w_3 = 8.60, w_4 = 15.60).
4. Scale weights by the nucleon parameters to yield baseline binding energies.
5. Apply exact categorical SU(4) anomaly splits to resolve degeneracies (e.g., 3H vs 3He).

Correctness conditions

These are fit residuals of the experimental model, not derived error bounds:

  1. With the seed constants calibrated, the generating function reproduces ^4He (n=4) to within \sim 3.4 keV of the AME value — a fit residual, not a parameter-free bound (^4He remains open, the \mathrm{Vol}_4 census gap).
  2. The isospin anomaly correction resolves the n=3 doublet ordering (^3H vs ^3He); the residual is a calibrated near-match, not an accuracy claim against the L2 target.

The q-lift of the depth-2 kernel. The q-lift of the proved classical depth-2 kernel exists exactly on the [n]_q!-normalized carrier (c(q) = 1, probe-verified; not yet formalized in Lean) and is distinct from the Garoufalidis–Gu–Mariño resurgent-Stokes carrier [garoufalidis-gu-marino2021] up to scalar gauge. The identification is open.

Scope (value proved; magnitude open, not a closure). The per-partition \Delta_\lambda value is proved (\Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda, sorry-free general-n, dtEuler_eq_deltaLambda_unconditional); what remains open is the many-body binding magnitude: six ansätze have failed on the deuteron magnitude r^\ast \approx 1.585, which no per-block \Delta_\lambda can supply. This module is an experimental / phenomenological generating-function model for that magnitude: the depth-2 CKRecursion reproduces the multi-body binding hierarchy from a small set of seed constants (r_{\mathrm{res}} \approx 2.596, a_0 = 1/2, the isospin anomaly shift \approx +1.4947\,m_e) that are calibrated, not derived from the 13 categorical drivers. It is a structural fit, not a parameter-free derivation.

Python API entry point

from qou_mass.api import predict          # the .ts manifest's declared entry point

# NOTE (corrected 2026-08-25, PR #5765): this block previously pointed at
# `computations.mass_binding_dashboard._row`. That module HAS `_row`, but it has
# ZERO occurrences of `B_unified` — the `B_unified` model lives in
# `computations/probes/strong_unified_binding_probe.py`, which emits no witness.
# The entry point above now matches `computation.script` in the .ts manifest.

Witness contract

Witness: computations/canonical-mass-table-242ppb.witness.json, as declared by computation.witness in this block's .ts manifest.

Corrected 2026-08-25 (PR #5765). This contract previously named dashboard_and_sweep_results.md, which does not exist anywhere in the repo (find → 0 hits) and disagreed with the .ts manifest. Two things a consumer should know about the witness that is declared:

  • It carries no provenance: computedAt, commitSha, witness.scriptHash, witness.scriptFile and witness.scriptCommitSha are all null, so no staleness check can key on it and no producer can be resolved from it. It is marked auditOnly.
  • Its numbers are not the live pipeline's. It records D +23 %, T +6 %, ³He +13 %, ⁴He +3.6 % — i.e. over-binding — computed at the 242-ppb nucleon level that the 2026-07-04 audit identified as a fitted-Habiro regression and removed. The live mass_binding_dashboard under-binds: ²H −27.5 %, ³H +38 %, ³He +44 %, ⁴He +69 % (err sym 0.79 / 1.38 / 1.44 / 3.26). Do not cite the witness figures as this step's current accuracy.

Notes

This module explores a q-difference generating-function route to the multi-body binding hierarchy. It does not supersede the \Delta_\lambda closure search, which is open. The shared CKRecursion shape across the weak (Q_\beta) and strong (binding) sectors is a structural observation / working hypothesis, not a proven identity. Axiomatisation is not proof: no c_k or \Delta_\lambda value produced here is carried downstream, pending a genuine closed-form derivation from the categorical drivers.

The CKRecursion recurrence is extensive and algebraically convenient, but its seed constants are calibrated inputs, so the binding it produces is a fit, not a derivation.

Tier note: experimental generating-function model

The w_n values and the \sim 3 keV ^4He fit residual come from the discrete q-difference recurrence with calibrated seeds — a phenomenological reproduction, not a structural bound. A kernel-constraints Lean file for the q-difference recurrence exists on the Q_\beta side (QBetaCKRecursionKernelConstraints.lean); a binding-sector analogue that would formalize any derived (non-calibrated) constant is not yet written.
